summary: Six bounded person entries deepen historiographical traditions beyond Europe and North America: Romila Thapar, Cheikh Anta Diop, Liang Qichao, Gu Jiegang, Ibn Khaldun and Masao Maruyama. Five new people records; Maruyama reuses his existing identity. Contributions, disputes, composition dates and modern translations remain distinct; the existing Maruyama modernization comparison keeps edge_735 and moves to his own entry. No general claim of systematic regional coverage.
authorization: User, 2026-10-24: address the supplied Gemini coverage feedback before returning to other work, and use sub-agents to split the work. Coordinator assigned this isolated six-person research batch. No publication or push authorized.
rationale: Each candidate has at least two substantive relationships, including the preserved Maruyama comparison, and at least three read-grounded dated contribution/writing points. Primary excerpts and later readers are explicitly distinguished; metadata-only extra titles cannot establish arguments or intellectual descent. Named disagreements are retained for Thapar, Diop, Liang, Gu and Maruyama, and colonial remakings of Ibn Khaldun are separated from medieval contexts. None is treated as the sole voice of a nation or tradition. Existing graph IDs, roster wording, historical qualifications and group edges are preserved except the declared individual Maruyama endpoint repair.
